19911-the-practical-values-of-space-expl:
The Practical Values of Space Exploration is a United States congressional report. It comes from the House Committee on Science and Astronautics. Its staff pages list special counsel, consultants, and clerks by name. Philip B. Yeager served as special consultant. John A. Carstarphen Junior was chief clerk. The report dates from the early space race, about 1960. Sputnik had pushed Congress to justify space spending.

Committees had to translate rockets into practical public value. Weather, communication, and science benefits fill such reports. This one preserves the official case at the program's dawn. Its staff lists show how Congress built space expertise. The document is a baseline for American space policy history.
doe-osti-2571209-stable-diacid-coordinat: Hot fuel cell polymers got their DOE report, and this text covers diacid-coordinated ammonium polymers for 80-230 C cells. The pages detail the chemistry. The fuel cell makers get their material. The cells were hot. The material was polymer. The chemistry was detailed.
doe-osti-3374169-ier-620-ced-3b-experime: PNDA got experiment-summarized, and this DOE IER-620 covers propylene die-away. The pages detail the pulsed findings. The nuclear folks get their data. The neutrons were pulsed. The data were nuclear. The PNDA were propylene. The CED-3b were IER-620.

Rachel Wilson takes the Rogan mic for episode 2460 of the Joe Rogan Experience, in a wide-ranging full-length talk. The episode is kept whole, so her views and stories arrive at her own pace rather than in clips chosen by others.

Across the sitting she holds forth on her ground, and Rogan draws her out in the show's open style. The transcript preserves the entire back-and-forth as aired. The entry serves listeners who want the complete appearance on file, a full record of one guest's hours in the chair, ready to be read or heard end to end.
the-return-of-peter-grimm:
An editor introduces David Belasco, born at San Francisco on July 25, 1853, as the Edison of the American stage. Belasco is praised as a creator with his own workshop, unlike contemporary managers described as manufacturers of amusement goods.

The portrait stresses his love of theatre, his willingness to take infinite pains for effect regardless of cost, and his skill at atmosphere and unified production. Only Winthrop Ames is said to rival his personal care. Readers meet the play through its producer's reputation, as a craftsman-manager carrying forward an older theatrical banner with new inventions.
